info.title: Connect current named application HTTP
info.description: Generated from real protocol serde DTOs in separate deserialize/serialize contexts and executable ApplicationOperation policy. Optional schema tooling is absent from production builds. Generation is not runtime, media, provider, host or remote qualification.

post.description: Explicit local application route. Framework JSON body parsing precedes bounded shared admission and bearer authentication. Canonical communication/control is deliberately excluded here. Current ordinary actors and verified narrow Task principals keep their own ceilings; X-Call-ID/X-Chat-ID do not create provider authority and are refused with Task principals. CORS only permits configured loopback browser origins; it is not authentication and does not make arbitrary headers trusted. Service/Store reauthorize current scope, membership, resource audience, expiry and immutable intent on replay. Administrator status is not private content access. Task request/step/reply attribution and original IDs remain distinct. Pairing proves Identity possession without SMS consent. Provider status/readiness are observations, not successful external effects or decoded media. The route adds no no-store header and has no route-wide absolute transaction deadline; named service waits and explicit SDK bounds retain their separate contracts.

200.description: Named result or typed business refusal. Inspect result.Err as well as status; invalid limits, changed intent, conflicts and pending/unknown effects need not change HTTP status.

401.description: Current ordinary credential or explicit verified Task principal missing, expired, revoked or malformed.

403.description: Current scope, resource, recipient, Task/grant/assurance or verified provider-header ceiling refused.

501.description: Recognized retired top-level command/action or an explicitly unsupported named capability. Use the canonical interface for retired calls; no fallback dispatch occurs.

503.description: Shared capacity exhausted or current authority/storage unavailable. Preserve original logical IDs and inspect acceptance after uncertainty.

400.description: Framework malformed JSON rejection before authentication.

413.description: Framework aggregate body limit before authentication: max(configured artifact_chunk_bytes,65536), default65536.

415.description: Framework JSON content type required before authentication.

422.description: Framework closed serde shape/type/enum/duplicate-field rejection before authentication.

post.x-schema-scope: Actual serde DTO shape and current top-level dispatch. Business normalization, cursor/ID/range limits, authorization and lifecycle are service policy; schema validity is not acceptance.

Explicit admission by a current manager with the named add capability.
Invitation/target acceptance remains a separate, opt-in workflow.

msg_id.description:
Canonical clients can choose their message identity independently of
the logical operation ID. Other clients use the accepted server ID.

transports.description: Only these transports may be considered; no implicit channel fallback.

Input_PrepareRequest.description:
The endpoint is resolved by the trusted native backend, then asserted again
under the same current Device/key fence. It is not a wire-selected grant.

oneOf.description:
Permit an attempt without claiming endpoint reachability. Known offline
or busy observations and all other prerequisites remain enforced.

Input_TaskCommand.description:
Administrative commands require backing actor authority; narrow invocation
grants may only use their bound task's communication/read operations.

oneOf.description:
A recipient answers a verified question using their own current send
authority. The store derives the task from the question reference.

operation.description:
Existing public operation; must match the enclosing logical request ID
and bound conversation. Administrative/nested operations are forbidden.

reply_to.description: Binds a question to an existing task reply; not an authority selector.

wait_for_reply.description:
Explicit question intent. The server waits for an attributed reply;
it never infers a question or task routing from message text.

oneOf.description:
Read bounded source projections from the task's existing conversation.
`after` is a task/reader-bound journal checkpoint, not an authority token.
History or context-view authority must remain current on every page.
Runner coordination only; possessing a worker ID does not confer authority.

Input_TaskDefinition.description: Developer-supplied task inputs. The authenticated actor supplies ownership.

initiating_event_id.description: Optional existing conversation event; its ownership is checked by the store.

Input_TaskPermission.description:
Closed set of delegatable communication operations and explicit bound-task
cancellation. Administrative authority and conversation creation are never
implicitly delegated; `TaskCancel` requires its own immutable ceiling.

oneOf.description: Explicit permission to include authorized record projections in context.

Explicit cancellation of only this delegated task. Never implied by
messaging, session control, status or any other communication permission.

Input_TaskRequest.description: Explicit versioned command carried by the task extension to control profile v1.

Input_TaskScope.description: Immutable authority ceiling; current actor/membership/route checks still apply.

sms_enrollments.description:
Explicit reviewed enrollment purposes for task-origin SMS. Empty denies
SMS dispatch without limiting the task's other communication channels.
Omit empty policy to preserve canonical digests of existing grants.

Input_TaskSmsEnrollment.description:
A reference to immutable evidence supplied by a trusted enrollment authority.
This reference neither enrolls a recipient nor renews or overrides consent.

Input_TaskState.description: A task remains attached to its conversation through waiting and restart.

oneOf.description: Native authenticated pairing verifies an identity only, never SMS consent.

Additive task policy carried by the existing control application. The
authenticated principal supplies ownership, never the request payload.

data.description: Standard padded base64. It is for bounded reliable artifact chunks, never audio.

path.description: Resolve against the configured Connect HTTP origin, never an arbitrary host.

state.description: `unknown` is returned once a stored observation expires.

Output_BrowserBinding.description: The server-selected browser route. A client must not confuse it with its UI selection.

end_requested.description: An accepted end intent remains visible until provider termination is known.

Output_Capabilities.description: Current caller-visible routes and permissions for a resolved participant.

availability.description: Only present when the caller has availability_get authority.

extensions.description:
Supported additive control profiles, not delegated permissions. Older
servers omit this field and therefore do not advertise task support.

participant_id.description:
Conversation appearance for participant-based routing; absent without
a selected Conversation. An Identity ID is not a Participant ID.

Output_CapabilityLimits.description: Public limits needed before sending a message, file or native audio frame.

Output_ComponentReadiness.description: One configured component. Reasons are stable codes, never provider errors.

configured.description:
False distinguishes omitted optional configuration from worker failure.
Older observations without this field describe configured components.

Output_ContactState.description: A configured address or caller ID never promotes this state to verified.

sms_consent.description: Always false: native pairing supplies no channel enrollment evidence.

Output_ContextDeliveryDestination.description: Captured native destination. This describes the original export and grants no access.

Output_ContextDeliveryLifecycle.description:
Observed control lifecycle, independent of media readiness. None means that
lane does not record an independently admitted cleanup phase.

Output_ContextDeliveryPage.description: Newest-first delivery receipts with an authenticated older-page cursor.

Output_ContextRecord.description:
Exact authorized record projection. Raw whole-record/manifest fingerprints
remain private to the server. This reference is data and grants no access.

deliveries_omitted.description: Older delivery receipts excluded from this recent snapshot. Page with context_deliveries.

Output_ConversationClosed.description: Original committed Conversation closure, shared by journal and typed hints.

Output_EffectState2.description: Dispatch uncertainty is persisted independently of the task lifecycle.

oneOf.description: Explicitly installed message connector, never a native media transport.

capabilities.description: Durable declared capability, independent of whether a client is online.

missing_ingress_observations.description: A missing receipt is explicit and never synthesized as a zero sample.

enqueue_full_observations.description: This queue was full at an enqueue, not an end-to-end loss estimate.

frame_age_boundary.description:
Age is sampled at dequeue before the corresponding handoff/write.
It excludes waiting inside the write and remote network/decoder time.

max_forwarded_frame_age_ms.description: Present only at stages enforcing a forwarding-age bound.

unit.description: Raw WebRTC queues carry track events; other stages carry frame packets.

Output_MutationReceipt.description:
A completed local mutation is distinct from provider/recipient delivery.
Task effects retain their own task-scoped status API instead of this reference.

Output_ObservationWork.description:
The committed question exported to this host-selected work context. These
labels are provenance, never a task grant, semantic answer or execution ID.

subscription_record_id.description:
Original explicit subscription that authorized a server reconciliation.
This is journal identity, not permission to access its media.

oneOf.description: Task results retain their own pending/uncertain semantics and provenance.

Output_OwnershipState.description: Authentication proves possession of a current native identity credential.

Output_Pairing.description: One-use challenge. The challenge appears only in the initiating owner's receipt.

refusal_code.description: Terminal refusal before external dispatch, when a connector cannot carry the content.

sms_decision.description: Dispatch eligibility decision, if this delivery uses SMS.

sms_grant_id.description: Opaque reference to the reviewed enrollment evidence used at dispatch.

local_media.description:
This control profile exposes no local native/media bridge. A provider
status cannot grant or manufacture a media-ready Connection.

participant_id.description:
Explicit intended Session recipient; provider Caller ID does not prove
that this Participant is the remote caller or has accepted the Session.

remote_identity_verified.description: Provider caller IDs and call state do not authenticate a remote principal.

Output_QuicSendBufferObservation.description: Shared physical-peer DATAGRAM byte occupancy, independent of packet queues.

accepted_datagrams.description: Quinn accepted a datagram; this does not prove remote receipt.

congestion_samples.description:
Samples at media sends; connection counters below are maxima across
sampled physical connections, never sums or measured network-loss rates.

Output_Readiness.description: Authenticated health diagnostic, sampled from this running process.

Output_ReadinessState.description: Local operational state; `ready` never promises remote end-to-end reachability.

recorded.description: None when the recipient's preferences suppress the report.

channel.description: Native and provider observations never upgrade one another.

Output_ReconciliationReference.description:
The Session control receipt records the policy decision. Follow this separate
operation for the actual bounded Connection reconciliation outcome.

Output_RecordAvailability.description:
A bounded hint, never a source grant or an assertion that audio was captured.
Fetch authenticates again and returns the digest of the caller's exact view.

Output_RouteCapability.description: A route configured by this installation. Configuration is not live reachability.

readiness.description: `configured` or `unconfigured`; never an assertion of carrier delivery.

Output_SessionEnded.description: Original terminal metadata, independent of later record finalization/retention.

Output_SessionJoinedParticipant.description: Immutable verified public appearance, independent of later role/name changes.

Output_SessionStarted.description:
Original activation snapshot. Later topology or codec changes do not rewrite
this fact; current state is obtained independently from a snapshot.

Output_SessionView.description:
Current shared Session metadata; live appearances and Connections are separate
scoped facts. No initiator/counterpart pair defines the Participant set.

Output_SipLeg.description: Durable intent and observed state for one SIP connection in a Session.

Output_SnapshotItem.description:
Current conversation topology and operation state. Message bodies and file
bytes remain separately paged by history and artifact APIs.

Output_TaskEffect.description: One effect identity includes its task, step and logical mutation.

error.description: Known rejection/delivery failure; uncertainty is represented by state.

Output_TaskEvent.description: Journal entry with stable source attribution and commit order.

Output_TaskEventData.description: Durable notification payload; authority is always rechecked when it is read.

Output_TaskOutcome.description: Public results shared by native, HTTP, language SDK and MCP adapters.

oneOf.description: Oldest-first recipient journal sources, at most 32 KiB serialized per page.

next.description: Last returned journal position. Reuse it to catch up after an empty page.

omitted.description:
Eligible entries after the input cursor not included in this page.
Missing bodies are separately explicit in each returned source's state.

oneOf.description:
Incoming message and explicit task assignment are committed before ACK.
A terminal/unavailable task may leave the retained reply unassigned.

Output_TaskPermission.description:
Closed set of delegatable communication operations and explicit bound-task
cancellation. Administrative authority and conversation creation are never
implicitly delegated; `TaskCancel` requires its own immutable ceiling.

oneOf.description: Explicit permission to include authorized record projections in context.

Explicit cancellation of only this delegated task. Never implied by
messaging, session control, status or any other communication permission.

Output_TaskRecord.description: Durable task metadata; revision is incremented on every lifecycle transition.

Output_TaskReply.description: A reply explicitly assigned to one task; unassigned history has no task ID.

Output_TaskScope.description: Immutable authority ceiling; current actor/membership/route checks still apply.

sms_enrollments.description:
Explicit reviewed enrollment purposes for task-origin SMS. Empty denies
SMS dispatch without limiting the task's other communication channels.
Omit empty policy to preserve canonical digests of existing grants.

Output_TaskSmsEnrollment.description:
A reference to immutable evidence supplied by a trusted enrollment authority.
This reference neither enrolls a recipient nor renews or overrides consent.

Output_TaskSource.description: Retained evidence is data, never an instruction that expands task authority.

actor_id.description: Empty only when a retained reference's underlying attribution is unavailable.

body.description:
Message text or current session/artifact metadata. Never artifact bytes,
server paths, or a replacement for an independently authorized file read.

created_at.description: None explicitly represents legacy sources with no recorded timestamp.

provenance.description: Journal event reference and projection/omission notes, never authority.

state.description: Available, deleted, expired or unavailable; unavailable sources have no body.

Output_TaskState.description: A task remains attached to its conversation through waiting and restart.

Output_TaskStepClaim.description:
A bounded step lease is an ownership hint, not permission to retry an effect.
Once an effect may have left the process, expiry requires reconciliation.

Output_TaskToolResult.description: A bounded tool result does not manufacture completion while the task is waiting.

Output_VideoProfile.description: Public capability limits for the named two-party VP8 profile.

Output_WebRtcVideoInputObservation.description:
Numeric observations before WebRTC VP8 normalization, without RTP bytes or IDs.
Sequence skips are local observations; they do not assert network packet loss.

Output_WriteDisposition.description: Local writer facts, never a remote delivery or consumption receipt.

ApplicationOperation.description: Current top-level named API. Nested Task Invoke retains the distinct full wire DTO and current Task policy. The schema describes serde shape; business validation/current authorization may still refuse.

Explicit admission by a current manager with the named add capability.
Invitation/target acceptance remains a separate, opt-in workflow.

RetiredTopLevelOperation.description: Shape-only reference for intentional HTTP501 refusals, including mixed membership/receipt branches. Never a fallback or a supported communication interface.

oneOf.description: Task results retain their own pending/uncertain semantics and provenance.

x-connect-generation-refinements: Serde externally tagged Result contains exactly one Ok/Err key.
Only top-level Outcome is narrowed; TaskEffect nested outcomes retain full attribution/recovery models.
Duplicate metadata JSON keys are refused by a custom serde byte decoder; parsed JSON Schema cannot express duplicate keys.
